confirmed.summary: FULL-mode booking always throws: executeBooking calls create_manual_viewing inside withAgency, but withAgency (packages/db/client.ts:35-38) sets only app.current_agency_id — never app.current_user_role — and the live create_manual_viewing RPC does PERFORM require_role('agent'), whose live definition raises 'no_role_context' (P0001) when that GUC is unset. Verified against the live DB (pg_get_functiondef of both functions).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Full mode, one pending action, buyer says 'yes': turn.ts:97 -> deps.executeBooking (process-turn-db.ts:200-204) -> create_manual_viewing raises P0001 'no_role_context'; the catch at process-turn-db.ts:223-227 only maps code 23P01, so it rethrows -> runTurn throws -> processTurnDb throws -> the drain catch leaves the row 'processing' and it retries forever (see the throw-path finding). No booking can EVER execute through the engine as written; the deterministic booking path — the whole point of the pre-step — is dead on arrival.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In executeBooking's transaction, set the role GUC before calling the RPC (e.g. SELECT set_config('app.current_user_role','aivena_staff',true) — require_role has an explicit aivena_staff bypass — or add an engine-scoped SECURITY DEFINER wrapper), and extend the catch to convert require_role/validation P0001s into {ok:false,reason:'action_invalid'} instead of rethrowing.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced logically end-to-end against both the worktree code and the live DB. (1) In full mode, turn.ts:97 routes a confirmed pending action through runActionTool, whose 'execute' branch (modes.ts:96-97, dispatchDecision full/commitment='execute') awaits executeBooking with no catch. (2) executeBooking (process-turn-db.ts:187-229) runs create_manual_viewing inside withAgency, and withAgency (packages/db/client.ts:35-38) sets ONLY app.current_agency_id; a repo-wide grep shows app.current_user_role is set only in the HTTP agencyContextMiddleware and admin/agencies.ts — never in the worker path — and the prepared migration has zero references to require_role/current_user_role/create_manual_viewing. (3) Live pg_get_functiondef confirms create_manual_viewing does PERFORM public.require_role('agent') and require_role raises 'no_role_context' ERRCODE P0001 when the GUC is NULL/empty; pg_db_role_setting shows no role- or database-level default for app.current_user_role that could rescue it. (4) The catch at process-turn-db.ts:223-227 maps only '23P01', so P0001 rethrows through runTurn and processTurnDb. (5) The drain's catch (outbox-worker.ts:54-58) only logs — the row stays 'processing' — and pick_and_claim_amanda_inbound (migration lines 270-285) re-steals stale-lease processing rows with NO attempts cap in its WHERE clause (MAX_ATTEMPTS is checked only in the worker's non-throw branch), so the row is re-claimed every ~120s and throws identically forever. No refutation path found: full-mode engine booking can never succeed as written.
confirmed.corrected_fix: In executeBooking's withAgency transaction (process-turn-db.ts), before the create_manual_viewing call, set the transaction-local GUCs the RPC checks: SELECT set_config('app.current_user_role','aivena_staff',true), set_config('app.current_user_id','amanda_engine',true) — require_role has an explicit aivena_staff bypass (verified in the live definition), and app.current_user_id feeds the booking's created_by audit field (otherwise it records 'system_create_manual_viewing'). Then broaden the catch: keep code '23P01' → {ok:false, reason:'slot_taken'}; map code 'P0001' (create_manual_viewing validation failures such as viewing_time_in_past / lead_not_found / property_not_found, plus any residual role-context error) → {ok:false, reason:'action_invalid'} while logging the Postgres error message (constraint/message name only, never bind params) so a genuine config regression stays visible in telemetry; rethrow everything else. Separately (companion throw-path finding), the drain should mark a thrown row pending-with-backoff or failed rather than leaving it 'processing', since pick_and_claim has no attempts cap for stale-lease steals.

confirmed.summary: In approval/assisted mode, the confirmation pre-step queues the literal placeholder '[confirm booking <echo>]' as a dashboard_tasks 'suggested_reply' (turn.ts:99 -> process-turn-db.ts queueDraft:261-283), and the live approve_dashboard_task RPC (verified) sends any suggested_reply task's text verbatim to the lead over WhatsApp — so the agent's 'one-tap approve' texts the buyer '[confirm booking Friday 28 August, 17:00 · Chalet IC-28746]' and never books anything.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Assisted mode, buyer taps/says yes to a slot: runActionTool('assisted','commitment') -> queue_one_tap -> deps.queueDraft('[confirm booking ...]','one_tap'). queueDraft writes task_type 'suggested_reply' with raw_payload.suggested_reply = the bracket string and no pending_action_id anywhere in the payload. Agent approves in /tasks -> approve_dashboard_task enqueues that string into send_queue -> buyer receives the raw placeholder; amanda_pending_actions row stays status='pending'; the viewing is never created. In approval mode it is worse: the pre-step queues this placeholder AND the reply dispatch queues a second draft — two approvable tasks for one inbound, one of which is the placeholder.
confirmed.suggested_fix: One-tap booking confirmations need their own task_type (not 'suggested_reply') carrying pending_action_id, plus an approval endpoint that executes the booking; until that exists, the pre-step must not route commitment confirmations through queueDraft.
confirmed.verdict_reason: CONFIRMED, with one corrected transmission detail. Verified in code: assisted/commitment -> queue_one_tap (modes.ts:58) and approval/commitment -> queue_draft (modes.ts:56) both land in turn.ts:97-100's queueDraft('[confirm booking <echo>]', kind), which process-turn-db.ts:261-283 writes as an ordinary task_type='suggested_reply' dashboard_tasks row with NO pending_action_id; greps prove draft_kind/'one_tap' is consumed nowhere (only the golden harness) and no route or dashboard surface references amanda_pending_actions — there is no one-tap executor, so the pending action stays 'pending' until expiry and the viewing is never created. Verified live (read-only): approve_dashboard_task sends COALESCE(p_edited_body, v_task.message_body) verbatim to send_queue/WhatsApp for any pending suggested_reply task. The approval-mode double-task claim is also confirmed (pre-step queue_draft + reply dispatch queue_draft = two approvable tasks per inbound). Corrected detail: the RPC sends message_body, not raw_payload.suggested_reply — and queueDraft writes the buyer's INBOUND text into message_body (draft only into raw_payload.suggested_reply), while the composer prefills/submits message_body (conversations.ts:43,66; inbox-workspace sendSuggestedAction). So the default one-tap approve echoes the buyer's own message back to them rather than texting the bracket placeholder — still zero booking, still critical, and it additionally breaks EVERY engine-queued reply draft in approval mode (live convention verified: 13/18 existing tasks have message_body == the AI draft, 0 == inbound). Corroborating: turn.ts:135's 'awaiting final one-tap approval' context branch is unreachable (bookingEcho never set in the queued path), so the model re-asks a question the buyer already answered while the phantom task sits in /tasks.
confirmed.corrected_fix: Two fixes, both required. (1) Booking confirmations must not ride queueDraft/'suggested_reply': give one-tap bookings their own task_type (e.g. 'amanda_booking_confirm') carrying pending_action_id in raw_payload, excluded from approve_dashboard_task (its task_type<>'suggested_reply' guard already refuses it — rely on that, and build a dedicated approval endpoint that calls the same deterministic executeBooking path, marks the pending action executed, and then sends the warm confirmation text). Until that endpoint exists, assisted mode should treat commitment like approval-mode reply (or escalateToHuman) rather than emitting a placeholder task that can neither book nor be safely approved; also fix the turn.ts:135 context so the queued case actually tells the buyer the slot is being locked in (today that branch is unreachable). (2) Independently, queueDraft must write the DRAFT text into dashboard_tasks.message_body (matching the live convention message_body = the AI draft; keep the inbound text in raw_payload.inbound_body_text) — as written, every approval-mode approve sends the buyer's own inbound message back to them verbatim via approve_dashboard_task's COALESCE(p_edited_body, v_task.message_body).

confirmed.summary: Thrown errors bypass MAX_ATTEMPTS and backoff entirely: the catch at outbox-worker.ts:54-58 leaves the row status='processing', the RPC's stale-lease branch (migration line 274) re-claims it every ~120s, and attempts — though incremented on every claim — is only consulted on the outcome.result==='retry' path (line 42). Any persistently-throwing row retries forever with zero backoff, burning full model-token cost each cycle.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Anthropic returns 500/overloaded (llm.ts:31-34 throws), or a turn hits any of the uuid-cast crashes below, or sendReply throws 'lead_has_no_phone' (process-turn-db.ts:245): processTurnDb throws -> catch logs, row stays 'processing' -> 120s later pick_and_claim steals the stale lease, attempts=2,3,4...∞ -> each cycle re-runs the full agent loop (up to 6 Sonnet calls + Haiku verifier). One poisoned row = a permanent ~30 model-calls/hour money leak per row, and the row never reaches 'failed'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the catch, apply the same exhaustion/backoff UPDATE as the retry path (status pending/failed by attempts, next_attempt_at backoff); also make the exhaustion check inside the RPC or gate claiming on attempts <= MAX_ATTEMPTS.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced logically end-to-end from the code: (1) the catch at outbox-worker.ts:54-58 performs no row UPDATE, so a thrown error leaves status='processing' with a ~120s lease; (2) the RPC's stale-lease branch (migration line 274) reclaims any expired 'processing' row with no attempts cap, incrementing attempts on every claim; (3) MAX_ATTEMPTS is only consulted on the outcome.result==='retry' path — and processTurnDb NEVER returns 'retry' (only 'skip'/'done'), while turn.ts/agent-loop.ts have zero try/catch around model calls, so every transient failure is a throw and the exhaustion/backoff branch is unreachable for real failures; (4) persistent throw sources exist: llm.ts throws on Anthropic non-OK/timeout and on missing key (amanda_llm_key_unavailable, a standing config error), and sendReply throws 'lead_has_no_phone' (process-turn-db.ts:245) AFTER the full agent loop already ran, so full Sonnet+Haiku token cost is burned each ~120s reclaim cycle (~30 cycles/hour — the finding actually understates worst case at up to ~7 model calls per cycle); (5) no other code path ever transitions processing→failed (grep confirms only the worker's two updates + the claim RPC touch the table; the old-rows sweep is deferred to P1 and is only an alert). The send_queue/turn_usage idempotency keys prevent duplicate outbound sends but do not prevent re-running the agent loop. Severity critical stands: unbounded model spend per poisoned row plus rows that never reach 'failed' and thus never surface.
confirmed.corrected_fix: Two layers, both needed. (a) Worker: in the catch at outbox-worker.ts:54-58, run the same exhaustion/backoff UPDATE as the retry path — best-effort, wrapped so a DB error there cannot kill the drain: `await withAgency(row.agency_id, tx => tx.execute(sql\`UPDATE public.amanda_inbound_queue SET status = ${row.attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS ? 'failed' : 'pending'}, next_attempt_at = now() + make_interval(secs => ${backoffSeconds(row.attempts)}), lease_expires_at = NULL, error_message = ${msg.slice(0,240)} WHERE id = ${row.id}::uuid\`)).catch(logOnly)`. (b) Defense-in-depth in the RPC (pick_and_claim_amanda_inbound): instead of merely gating the stale-steal on attempts (which would leave over-limit rows wedged in 'processing' forever), have the claim CTE first flip exhausted stale rows to failed — e.g. before the claiming UPDATE add: `UPDATE public.amanda_inbound_queue SET status='failed', lease_expires_at=NULL, error_message=coalesce(error_message,'max_attempts_exceeded') WHERE status='processing' AND lease_expires_at < now() AND attempts >= 5;` and add `AND q.attempts < 5` (matching MAX_ATTEMPTS; keep the constant in one place or pass it as a parameter) to both branches of the claim WHERE. This guarantees a persistently-throwing row reaches 'failed' within MAX_ATTEMPTS claims even if the worker process dies mid-row, and restores real backoff for transient Anthropic errors.

confirmed.summary: Text-confirmed booking is structurally unreachable in the normal case: proposeViewingSlots creates one pending action PER slot and always proposes up to 2 (backends-db.ts:150-152,171-193), the pre-step only auto-considers a pending action when EXACTLY one exists (process-turn-db.ts:150-160), buttons can never arrive (the engine sends via send_queue template_key 'freeform', and the live whatsapp-send-execute freeform path is plain Body — no interactive buttons), and nothing ever narrows 2 pending actions to 1 — both share the same 24h expiry.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Turn 1: model proposes Friday+Saturday (2 pending actions, 2 holds). Turn 2: buyer 'Friday at 17 works' -> pendingActions.length===2 -> pending=null, pendingNote tells the model to re-ask for explicit confirmation of that slot. Turn 3: buyer 'yes, confirmed' -> STILL 2 pending actions -> pre-step skipped again -> model re-asks again. Infinite confirmation loop; detectConfirmation is never even invoked. The design's preferred button path (design §4 line 62) does not exist in the send stack, and its fallback is gated on a count that the proposer itself guarantees is 2.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When the buyer's text names one of the open proposals, supersede the sibling(s) so exactly one remains for the next confirmation turn (deterministic label/weekday match in code, or a supersede-siblings step when the model restates a single slot); or propose one slot per pending-action round.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced end-to-end from code. (a) backends-db.ts:150-152 caps free slots at 2 and 171-193 inserts one amanda_pending_actions row per slot, both with now()+24h expiry in the same tx — identical expiry, so the pair never decays to one. (b) process-turn-db.ts:150-160 sets pending=null whenever pendingActions.length>1 and no button matches; runTurn (turn.ts:91-93) invokes detectConfirmation/executeBooking only when pending is non-null, and detectConfirmation(text,lang) has no slot-picking ability. (c) The engine's sendReply enqueues send_queue template_key 'freeform' (process-turn-db.ts:251); whatsapp-send-execute's freeform path sends plain Body (index.ts:354, no ContentSid), and only Content-API templates can carry quick-reply buttons that yield Twilio ButtonPayload — so the design's preferred button postback (DESIGN §4 line 62) is unreachable in this send stack. (d) The only sibling-supersede in the codebase is inside executeBooking's success path (process-turn-db.ts:213-216) — circular, since booking requires the exactly-one precondition; no trigger, sweep, or model tool (tools.ts registry has no book/confirm/release tool) narrows 2→1, and a re-proposal on a later turn adds rows (2→4). (e) The golden suite masks it: harness pending() injects a single PendingActionView straight into runTurn, bypassing the DB selection step; no scenario chains proposal-turn → DB-loaded confirmation-turn. Only quibble: 'infinite loop' overstates slightly (ends in buyer frustration/handoff or 24h expiry; a crowded calendar yielding exactly 1 free slot is a degenerate escape) — but text-confirmed booking being structurally unreachable in the normal 2-slot case stands, and it is the engine's core money path, so critical severity is warranted.
confirmed.corrected_fix: Keep 2-slot proposals (good UX, per design) and add a deterministic narrowing step in process-turn-db.ts before the pending-action selection: when pendingActions.length>1, match the inbound text against each action's stored label components (weekday name in the lead's language + day number + hour, from payload->>'label'/slot); if exactly one action matches, supersede the sibling(s) via the existing releasePendingAction('superseded') path (also deleting their viewing_slot_holds) and pass the survivor as the single PendingActionView with a note that this is the buyer's pick awaiting explicit confirmation — detectConfirmation then governs the next turn exactly as designed. If zero or >1 match, keep today's re-ask behavior. Additionally extend the golden harness with a two-turn scenario that runs the real selection logic (2 DB-style pending actions → buyer names one → supersede → 'yes' → booked) so the DB-side count law is exercised. Longer-term (P1): send proposals via a registered quick-reply template through the existing ContentSid path with ButtonPayload=pending_action_id, restoring the design's preferred button flow.

confirmed.summary: Model-supplied property_id / rejected_property_id are cast ::uuid with no validation, and no layer catches a throwing backend (executeToolCall and agent-loop.ts:74 have no try/catch around executeReal) — a model that passes the ref 'IC-28746' (which get_property_details explicitly trains it to use) crashes the whole turn; a bad rejected_property_id is persisted into amanda_lead_state and then poisons EVERY future searchProperties for that lead via string_to_array(...)::uuid[] (backends-db.ts:89).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Model calls propose_viewing_slots{property_id:'IC-28746'} -> backends-db.ts:178 '${propertyId}::uuid' -> 22P02 invalid uuid -> throw propagates through runActionTool/executeToolCall/runAgentLoop -> processTurnDb throws -> infinite-retry loop (finding above). Worse: record_lead_intel{rejected_property_id:'IC-28746'} succeeds (tools.ts:251 accepts any string, stored in state jsonb); from then on every search_properties for this lead throws on the uuid[] cast — the lead's conversation is permanently broken across all future turns.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Validate uuid shape at the tool boundary (refuse('invalid_property_id') like missing_ref), resolve refs to ids server-side, and wrap executeReal so a backend throw becomes a refused ToolEvent instead of a turn crash.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced logically end-to-end in the code. (1) tools.ts:200 validates property_id only as non-empty string; backends-db.ts:178 casts ${propertyId}::uuid in the amanda_pending_actions INSERT, so a ref like 'IC-28746' raises 22P02 in full mode — and ask_agency's property_id hits the same unvalidated cast (backends-db.ts:212) executing for real from approval mode up, wider than the finding claims. No layer contains the throw: modes.ts:97 runActionTool awaits executeReal bare, executeToolCall has no try/catch, agent-loop.ts:74 none, turn.ts none, processTurnDb none; it lands in drainAmandaInbound's catch (outbox-worker.ts:54) which performs NO row update — the row stays 'processing', the 120s lease expires, pick_and_claim (no attempts<MAX filter, steals stale leases) re-claims it, and the exhaustion→'failed' branch only fires on a returned retry outcome, never a throw → genuine infinite retry burning model tokens each cycle. (2) record_lead_intel accepts any string as rejected_property_id (tools.ts:251), mergeExtraction persists it unvalidated into amanda_lead_state jsonb (executes real from approval mode up); every later turn loads it unvalidated (process-turn-db.ts:178) and backends-db.ts:89 string_to_array(...)::uuid[] throws 22P02 on every search_properties for that lead — and since read tools execute for real in EVERY mode including shadow (modes.ts:52), the lead's turns crash in all modes with no self-healing path. Likelihood is plausible: nothing in tool schemas or prompt.ts steers the model to the uuid id, get_property_details' description circulates the ref format, and the prompt injects rejected ids verbatim into context. Only nuance: propose_viewing_slots itself crashes only in full mode (approval/assisted queue without executing), but ask_agency and the poisoning path fire from approval up, so the substance holds across the dial.
confirmed.corrected_fix: Three layers: (1) At the tool boundary (tools.ts), validate uuid shape for property_id / rejected_property_id with a UUID_RE and refuse('invalid_property_id') like the existing missing_ref refusals; optionally resolve refs to ids server-side (getPropertyDetails already matches external_id OR id::text — reuse that lookup) so a ref-passing model still succeeds. (2) In executeToolCall (or runActionTool's execute branch), wrap executeReal in try/catch and convert a throw into { ok:false, refused:'backend_error' } so one bad tool call becomes a model-visible error instead of a turn crash. (3) Defense in depth: filter ctx.rejectedPropertyIds to uuid-shaped strings when loading in process-turn-db.ts:178 (heals already-poisoned amanda_lead_state rows), and make drainAmandaInbound's catch block write the failure to the row (increment-aware status/next_attempt_at update) so a throwing row can actually exhaust to 'failed' instead of retrying forever on lease expiry.

confirmed.summary: Lease steal mid-turn is guaranteed under load: engineTick runs on a bare 20s setInterval with no in-flight guard (index.ts:229), while one drain claims up to 20 rows with a single 120s lease at claim time (outbox-worker.ts:22-24) and then processes them sequentially, each turn legitimately taking up to ~6×45s of model calls (agent-loop.ts:38, llm.ts:16) plus verifier and regeneration — so rows late in a batch (or any single slow turn) outlive their lease and are re-claimed by an overlapping tick in the same process.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Batch of 5 rows where row 1's turn takes 150s: rows 2-5 sit leased-but-unprocessed past 120s; the next tick's pick_and_claim steals them (stale-lease branch) and processes them while drain #1 eventually reaches them too. Consequences per duplicated row: double model spend; duplicate dashboard_tasks drafts (queueDraft has no idempotency key); two concurrent executeBooking calls on the same pending action (the SELECT at process-turn-db.ts:189-196 takes no row lock) where the loser's 'slot just taken — apologize' reply can win the send_queue idempotency race while the booking actually succeeded; and the loser's unconditional status UPDATE (outbox-worker.ts:43-50, WHERE id only — no status/lease guard) can flip an already-'done' row back to 'pending' for a third run.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Guard reentrancy (skip tick while a drain is in flight), lease per-row at processing time or renew mid-turn, size the lease to worst-case turn duration × batch, add FOR UPDATE on the pending-action select, and make the completion UPDATE conditional on status='processing' AND the worker's own lease.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Every load-bearing claim reproduces from the code and live DB. index.ts:229 runs engineTick on a bare 20s setInterval with no in-flight guard, so overlapping drains in one process are real. outbox-worker.ts:21-24 claims up to 20 rows with one 120s lease stamped at claim time (RPC at migration lines 262-287, whose stale-steal branch re-claims processing rows past lease; FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED is irrelevant because the claim tx commits immediately and drain #1 holds no locks while processing). A turn can legitimately take ~330s (agent-loop.ts:38 MAX_ITERATIONS=6 x llm.ts:16 45s timeout, + regeneration at turn.ts:161 + two 8s verifier calls), and no lease renewal or ownership token exists (leased_by is the constant 'api-worker'), so rows late in a batch — or a single slow turn's own row — outlive the lease and get stolen and double-processed. Consequences verified: double model spend; duplicate dashboard_tasks drafts (queueDraft at process-turn-db.ts:261-283 is a plain INSERT; live DB shows only the pkey unique index); the pending-action SELECT at process-turn-db.ts:189-196 takes no row lock, so two concurrent executeBooking calls race — the migration's bookings_active_slot_exclusive EXCLUDE makes the loser get 23P01 -> slot_taken -> the "slot just taken, apologize" context (turn.ts:107-115, which also supersedes the action), and since both runs share the same send_queue idempotency key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, the loser's contradictory apology can be the one reply that actually sends while the booking exists; and the completion UPDATEs (outbox-worker.ts:33-39 and 43-50) are WHERE id only with no status/lease guard, so a loser's retry outcome flips an already-done row back to pending for a third run. No mitigating mechanism (lease re-check, renewal, reentrancy guard, worker identity) exists anywhere in the worker path.
confirmed.corrected_fix: The suggested fix is directionally correct; refine it in four parts. (1) Reentrancy: skip a tick while a drain is in flight (simple boolean latch around engineTick), which removes same-process overlap but NOT cross-instance overlap during deploys — so the DB-side guards below are still required. (2) Lease integrity: give each drain a unique claim token (e.g. leased_by = worker uuid per drain instead of the constant 'api-worker'), renew the lease per row just before processing it (UPDATE ... SET lease_expires_at = now()+lease WHERE id = $1 AND status='processing' AND leased_by = $token RETURNING id — a miss means the row was stolen: skip it without processing), and make BOTH completion UPDATEs conditional on status='processing' AND leased_by = $token so a stolen row's stale worker can neither double-complete nor flip done back to pending. This per-row renewal also fixes the batch-wide-lease sizing problem better than inflating the lease to worst-case-turn x batch (which would delay legitimate crash recovery by ~90 minutes). (3) Booking: add FOR UPDATE to the pending-action SELECT at process-turn-db.ts:189-196 so the loser serializes and re-evaluates status='pending' after the winner commits (returning action_invalid instead of attempting a duplicate insert); note this alone still yields a contradictory apology draft, so the real protection is (2) preventing the duplicate turn from running at all, plus optionally distinguishing action_invalid (already executed — confirm warmly) from slot_taken (genuinely lost — apologize) in turn.ts. (4) Draft idempotency as defense-in-depth: key queueDraft on the turn id (e.g. unique index on (raw_payload->>'via', raw_payload->>'inbound_message_id') scoped to amanda_engine, or a dedicated turn_id column) so a residual duplicate run cannot produce duplicate dashboard cards, mirroring the send_queue idempotency_key pattern already used in sendReply.

confirmed.summary: The 'awaiting final one-tap approval by the office — tell them it is being locked in' context (turn.ts:135) is dead code: it requires bookingEcho set with no bookingId/wouldBook, but the queued branch (result.queued from approval/assisted commitment dispatch) sets neither bookingEcho nor clears effectivePending (turn.ts:101-121), so after queueing the one-tap the model still sees the ORIGINAL unconfirmed proposal echo.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Assisted mode, buyer 'Yes please!': one-tap queued, then the model is prompted with <pending_viewing_proposal>Friday 28 August, 17:00 · Chalet IC-28746</pending_viewing_proposal> plus the buyer's yes — nothing tells it the confirmation was accepted, so it plausibly re-asks 'shall I book it?' or claims it is booked (golden S8 hides this by scripting the ideal reply). And because the pending action stays status='pending' in the DB, the buyer's next 'yes' runs the pre-step again and queues a SECOND one-tap task for the same slot.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the queued branch, set bookingEcho = pendingAction.echo and clear effectivePending (making line 135's one-tap message reachable), and mark the pending action e.g. status='confirmed' so a repeat affirmation doesn't re-queue.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced logically from the code. (1) Dead code: bookingEcho is only ever set at turn.ts:104-105 (with bookingId) or 117-119 (with wouldBook=true), so line 135's ternary condition `bookingId || wouldBook` is always true when bookingEcho is truthy — the 'awaiting final one-tap approval' string is unreachable. (2) modes.ts maps assisted×commitment→queue_one_tap and approval×commitment→queue_draft (both `queued` set, `simulated` false), which falls through both branches at turn.ts:101/116, leaving bookingEcho=null and effectivePending=the original proposal — the model is prompted with the unchanged <pending_viewing_proposal> despite prompt.ts:55 promising it 'the system... will tell you when that happened'. Golden S8 scripts the ideal reply so the gap is invisible to tests. (3) The queued path never touches amanda_pending_actions (executeBooking/releasePendingAction not called) and queueDraft in process-turn-db.ts:261-283 is a plain INSERT into dashboard_tasks with no idempotency, so the row stays status='pending', loadWorld reloads it next turn, and a repeat affirmation queues a duplicate one-tap task. Mitigating fact verified: no double booking can result — executeBooking filters status='pending' and supersedes siblings, so a second tap gets action_invalid; the impact is duplicate agent tasks + a model re-asking after the buyer already said yes, consistent with 'important' severity.
confirmed.corrected_fix: In turn.ts's pre-step, handle the queued case explicitly: `else if (result.queued) { bookingEcho = pendingAction.echo; effectivePending = null; }` — line 135's else-branch then becomes reachable (bookingId null, wouldBook false), and its wording should cover both queued kinds (assisted one_tap AND approval draft), e.g. 'awaiting a quick approval by the office — tell them it is being locked in, do not re-ask'. To stop re-queueing, do NOT simply set status='confirmed' as suggested — that alone breaks the execution path, because executeBooking (process-turn-db.ts:194) and releasePendingAction (:236) filter on status='pending', and loadWorld (:78) would drop the action from context. Either (a) introduce a distinct status (e.g. 'buyer_confirmed') added to the migration's allowed statuses, load it alongside 'pending' in loadWorld so the pre-step can treat a re-affirmation as a no-op ('already awaiting office approval' context note), and widen executeBooking/releasePendingAction to accept it; or (b) keep status='pending' and stamp a marker (e.g. payload.buyer_confirmed_at) that loadWorld surfaces and the pre-step checks before queueing, plus an idempotency key on the one-tap dashboard_tasks insert (e.g. derived from pending_action_id) as a backstop. confirmed.summary: propose_viewing_slots is commitment-class, so in approval/assisted modes the model receives only a {queued:'draft'|'one_tap'} stub (modes.ts:54-58; tools.ts run() at 179-180 passes no queue callback) — no slot labels, no pending actions created — while the prompt orders it to echo returned slot labels; any times the model then invents pass every gate (gates.ts:36-41 excludes times from numeric grounding; the verifier explicitly allows 'scheduling chatter and times', llm.ts:66) and in assisted mode auto-send.

Keep shadow simulated as-is. confirmed.summary: The decline check is a bare word-scan that runs before the affirmative check (confirmation.ts:54-55): any message containing 'no'/'not' — including the common affirmations 'no problem', 'no worries', 'ok no problem', Spanish 'vale, no hay problema' — returns 'decline', which silently releases the pending action and deletes its holds (turn.ts:122-125) without telling the model a decline happened.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Amanda: 'Friday 28 August, 17:00 — does that work?' Buyer: 'Ok no problem'. detectConfirmation: words=['ok','no','problem'] -> 'no' ∈ NEGATIVES -> 'decline' -> releasePendingAction('declined'), holds deleted, effectivePending=null. The model sees no pending echo and no decline note, replies something generic; the buyer believes the viewing is agreed while the proposal is dead — nothing ever books and nobody is told.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Treat 'no problem'/'no worries'/'no pasa nada'/'no hay problema' as affirmative collocations before the NEGATIVES scan (or require the negative token to be standalone/leading), and pass a 'buyer declined the proposal' note into the model context when a decline does fire.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced end-to-end in code. confirmation.ts:55 runs the NEGATIVES word-scan before any affirmative check, and NEGATIVES contains bare 'no'/'not', so "Ok no problem" (normalize→"ok no problem", words ['ok','no','problem'], no MODIFIER_RE hit, under 60 chars) returns 'decline' — likewise "no worries", "vale, no hay problema", "no pasa nada". turn.ts:122-125 then calls releasePendingAction(id,'declined') and nulls effectivePending; the real backend (process-turn-db.ts:231-239) sets the pending action to 'cancelled' AND deletes its viewing_slot_holds rows. Because bookingEcho and effectivePending are both null, loopCtx.pendingActionEcho is null (turn.ts:134-136), so the model is told nothing — no pending echo, no decline note — and generates a generic reply while the proposal is dead and the hold is freed for other leads. A later buyer "yes" has nothing left to affirm. confirmation.test.ts covers only bare negatives ('no', 'mejor otro dia', "can't make it"), so nothing pins the collocation behavior. Severity 'important' is right: common affirmations silently kill bookings with a destructive DB side effect.
confirmed.corrected_fix: Two-part fix. (1) In detectConfirmation, before the NEGATIVES scan, strip known affirmative/neutral collocations from the normalized text — 'no problem', 'no worries', 'not a problem', 'no pasa nada', 'no hay problema', 'no te preocupes', 'geen probleem', 'kein problem', 'pas de probleme/problème', 'nessun problema', 'sem problema', 'inga problem' — then classify the remainder: "ok no problem" → "ok" → affirm; a bare "no problem" → empty remainder → treat as affirm only if the collocation is on an explicit affirmative-collocation list, else 'unclear' (re-ask), never 'decline'. This honors the file's own doctrine (a miss re-asks; only the negative verdicts carry side effects). (2) In turn.ts, when textVerdict === 'decline', do not silently null the context: after releasePendingAction, set effectivePending to a note like `${pendingAction.echo} — the buyer just DECLINED this proposed slot (it has been released): acknowledge gracefully and offer to find alternative times (propose_viewing_slots)` so the model's reply matches what the deterministic layer just did — this is needed even for genuine declines, independent of part (1). Add tests: 'ok no problem'/'no problem'/'no worries'/'vale, no hay problema' must not return 'decline', and a golden scenario asserting a decline turn produces a reply generated with the decline note in context.

confirmed.summary: proposeViewingSlots' availability check counts the engine's own just-created holds (backends-db.ts:161-167 matches ANY unexpired viewing_slot_holds row, agent_key is always 'agency'), so re-proposing within the 15-minute hold TTL sees the previously offered slots as busy and offers different days; executeBooking also only deletes the executed action's hold (process-turn-db.ts:212), leaving sibling holds to block those slots until TTL.

Buyer replies 3 minutes later 'Friday works' -> (per the 2-pending-action dead-end) the model re-proposes to pin the slot -> conflict check sees its own Friday/Saturday holds -> both skipped -> Amanda counter-offers Monday/Tuesday to a buyer who just accepted Friday.

confirmed.summary: amanda_questions has no UNIQUE (agency_id, short_code): the smallest-unused short_code is computed in a read-only CTE (backends-db.ts:200-215) with no serialization, so two concurrent askAgency calls for one agency can both mint the same code (both snapshots see 1 as unused).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Two turns for the same agency file questions in overlapping transactions -> both insert short_code 1 -> the §3b reply ladder ('Q1: ...' prefix matching, 'short-codes never recycled within 7 days') now has two live Q1s and an agent's answer can bind to the wrong buyer's question — exactly the mis-relay the design calls reviewer-critical.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add a partial unique index on (agency_id, short_code) over live/recent rows and retry code allocation on conflict.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced logically end-to-end: (1) migration lines 172-205 define amanda_questions with no UNIQUE/exclusion constraint on (agency_id, short_code) — only the id PK and three non-unique indexes; (2) backends-db.ts:200-215 mints the code via a read-only CTE + INSERT inside withAgency, which is a bare READ COMMITTED db.transaction (packages/db/client.ts:31-39) with no advisory lock, no ON CONFLICT, no retry — two overlapping transactions both snapshot code 1 as unused and both insert it; (3) the concurrency precondition is real: index.ts:229 runs engineTick on setInterval(20s) with no in-flight guard while a turn spans multiple LLM calls, and pick_and_claim_amanda_inbound (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, no per-agency fencing) lets an overlapping tick or a second instance (explicitly supported — "safe across instances", index.ts:218) claim different rows of the same agency and process them concurrently; (4) consequence matches the design contract: DESIGN_v1.2 §3b-spine makes the "Q3:" short-code prefix a binding rung of the deterministic reply ladder and mandates never-recycled-within-7-days + no-auto-relay-on-ambiguity — duplicate live Q1s silently defeat that ladder's ambiguity detection, and short_code is already user-facing in P0 (dashboard_tasks title "Amanda needs an answer (Q1)" backends-db.ts:227; prompt note process-turn-db.ts:121). Severity minor is fair: the mint transaction is short (narrow collision window) and the ladder itself is a P2 build, but the schema being applied now must carry the invariant since codes persist 7 days.
confirmed.corrected_fix: In the migration, add a partial unique index enforcing one live ticket per code: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX amanda_questions_live_code_uq ON public.amanda_questions (agency_id, short_code) WHERE status IN ('open','clarifying','escalated'); — note the original suggestion's "live/recent" predicate cannot include created_at > now() - interval '7 days' (now() is not IMMUTABLE, Postgres rejects it in index predicates), so the 7-day non-recycle rule stays enforced by the allocation query's WHERE clause as today. In backends-db.ts askAgency, wrap the allocation INSERT in a small retry loop (2-3 attempts) that catches unique_violation (23505) and re-runs the CTE+INSERT so the loser re-mints the next free code. Alternative (also fully protects the 7-day window with no schema change): take a per-agency transaction-scoped advisory lock before minting — SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('amanda_q:' || current_setting('app.current_agency_id', true))) — which serializes allocation per agency; ideally do both (lock for serialization, index as the invariant backstop).

confirmed.summary: recordLeadIntel is a read-modify-write without a row lock (backends-db.ts:243-253: SELECT state, merge in JS, upsert SET state=EXCLUDED.state) — concurrent turns for the same lead clobber each other's patches; version increments but the losing patch's data is gone.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Under the overlapping-tick/lease-steal condition, two concurrent turns both read state {}, one records budget_max, the other records areas; second committer overwrites the first — budget silently lost, and the re-ask blocker (slotFilled) later lets Amanda ask for the budget again.
confirmed.suggested_fix: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE before merging, or merge in SQL (state || excluded jsonb with per-slot timestamp comparison).
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced logically end-to-end. backends-db.ts:243-253 does SELECT state (no FOR UPDATE) → JS mergeExtraction → upsert SET state=EXCLUDED.state inside a plain READ COMMITTED withAgency tx, so a transaction that read before a concurrent writer committed blindly overwrites that writer's slots (version still increments, masking the loss). The precondition — two concurrent turns for the same lead — is genuinely reachable: index.ts:229 runs the drain via setInterval(20s) with no reentrancy guard while a drain (up to 20 rows × multi-LLM-call turns) routinely exceeds 20s, and pick_and_claim_amanda_inbound fences only per-row (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), never per-conversation — a lead's second message is claimable by the next overlapping tick mid-turn; the 120s lease steal adds a same-row duplicate route. No debounce/conversation-lease exists in the built code (README mentions one; it was not implemented). record_lead_intel executes for real in approval/assisted/full modes (modes.ts:54-61). Downstream effect matches: lost budget_max makes slotFilled false → §10 B2 re-ask blocker fails; rejected_property_ids union additions are lost the same way → possible re-pitch. Severity minor is right: the per-call race window is milliseconds and impact is behavioral (re-ask/re-pitch), not broad corruption.
confirmed.corrected_fix: The suggested SELECT ... FOR UPDATE serializes the update case but is incomplete for the first-write case (no row exists → nothing to lock → two first writers still race through ON CONFLICT and the loser's stale merge overwrites). Use one of: (a) pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(${ctx.leadId})) at the top of the withAgency tx before the SELECT (simplest, fully closes both cases), or (b) move the merge into SQL: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (lead_id) DO UPDATE SET state = merged expression over amanda_lead_state.state and EXCLUDED.state with per-slot 'at' timestamp comparison (and set-union for rejected_property_ids / append for promised_followups), so the DB row's committed value — not the JS snapshot — is always the merge base.

confirmed.summary: preferred_time_iso is a model-emitted absolute datetime (design §4 says the model never emits these; datetime-resolver.ts is dead code in the wired path), and Date.parse of a timezone-less ISO string (backends-db.ts:143) is interpreted in the SERVER's timezone (UTC on Railway), shifting the buyer's requested hour.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Buyer: 'viernes a las 17'. Model calls propose_viewing_slots{preferred_time_iso:'2026-08-28T17:00:00'} (no offset). Date.parse -> 17:00 UTC = 19:00 Europe/Madrid; the candidate passes the notice check and the (honest) label offers 'Friday 28 August, 19:00' — Amanda counter-offers a time two hours off the buyer's request instead of the one they asked for.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Route free-text time preferences through resolveDatetimePhrase with the agency timezone (its intended purpose), or reject tz-less ISO input and interpret model ISO only when it carries an explicit offset.
confirmed.verdict_reason: CONFIRMED by direct code reading and runtime reproduction. (1) tools.ts:91 exposes preferred_time_iso as a bare model-emitted string (no format/offset/timezone description) and tools.ts:203 passes it verbatim to backends.proposeViewingSlots — while DESIGN_v1.2 §4 line 63 states "the model NEVER emits absolute datetimes from relative phrases. A deterministic resolver (agency IANA tz, fresh now() each turn) converts". (2) grep proves resolveDatetimePhrase/parseTime are consumed ONLY by datetime-resolver.test.ts — the §4-mandated resolver is unwired in the turn path (the file's wallClockInZone/zonedTimeToUtc helpers are used, but the phrase resolver itself is dead). (3) Reproduced the exact failure: under TZ=UTC (Railway default), Date.parse('2026-08-28T17:00:00') = 17:00:00Z per ECMA-262 local-time rule for offset-less date-times, and slotLabel renders it in Europe/Madrid as "Fri 28 August, 19:00" — a 2h shift from the buyer's requested 17:00 (1h in winter). The shifted candidate needs only the notice check (backends-db.ts:144) and conflict check, is pushed FIRST so it becomes the headline offer, and notably bypasses viewingHoursByWeekday entirely, so an off-grid 19:00 is proposable. (4) Two aggravators found during verification: prompt.ts gives the model NO current datetime and NO agency timezone, so it cannot even compute a correct offset-bearing ISO for "viernes a las 17" (it must hallucinate the date too); and even a model that dutifully adds an offset would have to guess which one. Severity "minor" is right: the label is honest (derived from the actual instant), the buyer must still confirm the slot, and the graceful path (candidateSlots fallback) still runs — so no silently wrong booking, but Amanda counter-offers a time shifted from what the buyer asked, appearing to ignore their stated preference.
confirmed.corrected_fix: Preferred (matches design §4 and uses the already-built, already-tested resolver): change the tool input from preferred_time_iso to preferred_time_phrase (the buyer's verbatim words, e.g. "viernes a las 17"), and in backends-db.ts proposeViewingSlots call resolveDatetimePhrase(phrase, ctx.nowMs(), ctx.settings.timezone); on ok push r.utcISO's ms as the first candidate, on {reason:'ambiguous_time'|'missing_time'} surface a clarify signal in the tool result instead of a slot. Minimal alternative if the ISO input is kept for now: only accept preferred_time_iso when it carries an explicit offset (/(Z|[+-]\d{2}:?\d{2})$/) and Date.parse is finite; otherwise interpret the offset-less wall-clock via zonedTimeToUtc(...ctx.settings.timezone) rather than Date.parse — never let the server TZ decide. In either variant, also add the current date/time in the agency timezone to the prompt context if the model is expected to reason about relative dates at all.

confirmed.summary: The EF enqueues an amanda_inbound_queue row for EVERY agency including amanda_mode='off' (lines 248-269 gate only on finalStatus), while the worker only exists when AMANDA_ENGINE_ENABLED=true (index.ts:220) and there is no sweeper/retention — with the EF deployed ahead of the env flag (the stated rollout state), the queue grows unbounded and 'off'-agency rows are pure dead weight forever.

confirmed.summary: The bookings EXCLUDE constraint (lines 95-99) indexes the expression tstzrange(scheduled_at, scheduled_at + make_interval(...)) — but timestamptz + interval (timestamptz_pl_interval) is STABLE, not IMMUTABLE (verified live: pg_proc.provolatile = 's'; make_interval and tstzrange are 'i'). Index/EXCLUDE expressions require immutable functions, so this ALTER TABLE is rejected and the whole migration fails.

AS $$ SELECT tstzrange($1, $1 + make_interval(mins => COALESCE($2, 60)), '[)') $$` (safe: pure minutes arithmetic on timestamptz is timezone-independent), use booking_slot(scheduled_at, duration_minutes) in the EXCLUDE and in the proposeViewingSlots conflict probe (backends-db.ts:159). While touching it, wrap the COALESCE element in extra parens `((COALESCE(agent_id, agent_name, 'agency')))` to stay clear of index_elem grammar edge cases (agent_id and agent_name are both text on live bookings, so the COALESCE itself type-checks; booking_status labels requested/confirmed/rescheduled in the WHERE all exist live).
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced end-to-end: migration lines 95-99 put tstzrange(scheduled_at, scheduled_at + make_interval(...)) in an EXCLUDE USING gist element on public.bookings; live DB confirms scheduled_at is timestamptz and pg_proc.provolatile='s' (STABLE) for timestamptz_pl_interval (make_interval/tstzrange are 'i'). EXCLUDE constraints build a GiST index and PostgreSQL requires every function/operator in an index expression to be IMMUTABLE — a STABLE operator function fails with 42P17 "functions in index expression must be marked IMMUTABLE", and volatility is per-function so the minutes-only interval does not exempt it. The statement therefore aborts the migration; everything after line 95 (bookings lifecycle columns, usage/lead-state/knowledge/questions/funnel tables, amanda_mode dial, claim RPC) never applies, and process-turn-db.ts:225's 23P01→slot_taken handling has no constraint to fire it. confirmed.corrected_fix: In the migration, before the ALTER TABLE, create an IMMUTABLE wrapper and use it in the EXCLUDE element: CREATE FUNCTION public.booking_slot(ts timestamptz, mins integer) RETURNS tstzrange LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE RETURNS NULL ON NULL INPUT AS $$ SELECT tstzrange(ts, ts + make_interval(mins => COALESCE(mins, 60)), '[)') $$ — wait, with STRICT a NULL duration would null the slot; instead keep it non-strict and COALESCE inside: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.booking_slot(ts timestamptz, mins integer) RETURNS tstzrange LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE AS $$ SELECT tstzrange(ts, ts + make_interval(mins => COALESCE(mins, 60)), '[)') $$; then EXCLUDE USING gist (agency_id WITH =, COALESCE(agent_id, agent_name, 'agency') WITH =, public.booking_slot(scheduled_at, duration_minutes) WITH &&) WHERE (...). Promoting to IMMUTABLE is safe here: minutes-only arithmetic on a timestamptz instant is timezone-independent (only day/month interval components are TZ-sensitive). confirmed.summary: MAX_ATTEMPTS and backoff are enforced only in the outcome.result==='retry' branch (lines 41-51), but processTurnDb never returns 'retry' (only 'done'/'skip' — it THROWS on any error). A thrown error hits the catch at line 54 which only logs: the row stays 'processing' and pick_and_claim_amanda_inbound (migration lines 270-285) steals it again when lease_expires_at passes — forever, attempts incrementing past MAX_ATTEMPTS with no cap and no backoff. Retries are not idempotent: each rerun re-executes real internal writes — askAgency files a NEW amanda_questions ticket + dashboard task + funnel event each time (backends-db.ts:198-238), proposeViewingSlots inserts NEW pending actions + holds each time (backends-db.ts:171-194) — and burns a full Sonnet loop + Haiku verifier per attempt.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Combined with the send_queue enum bug, EVERY assisted/full turn becomes a poison row: model loop runs, sendReply throws, row re-claimed every ~2 minutes indefinitely — duplicate office tickets pile up, duplicate viewing proposals pile up (so the confirmation law then always sees >1 pending action), and token spend is unbounded until someone notices. Any persistent model/API error (key revoked, model 404) does the same to every inbound row.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the catch, update the row like the retry branch does (attempts already incremented by the claim RPC): status='failed' when row.attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS else 'pending' with next_attempt_at = now() + backoffSeconds(row.attempts). Note next_attempt_at is only honored for status='pending' — the stale-lease steal ignores it, which is another reason the row must be flipped out of 'processing' on error.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced end-to-end in code + live DB. processTurnDb returns only 'done'/'skip' (never 'retry') and has no try/catch — model/DB errors throw; the worker catch (outbox-worker.ts:54-58) only logs, leaving the row status='processing'; the claim RPC's stale-lease steal branch (migration lines 270-285) has no attempts cap and ignores next_attempt_at, so the row is re-claimed every ~120s forever with attempts incrementing past MAX_ATTEMPTS and zero backoff. Non-idempotent side effects re-execute per attempt: askAgency files a new amanda_questions ticket + question event + dashboard task + funnel event each run (backends-db.ts:198-238, no idempotency key) and proposeViewingSlots inserts new pending actions + holds each run (171-194); a full Sonnet loop + Haiku verifier burns per attempt while amanda_turn_usage records only attempt 1 (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), hiding the spend. Live-DB check confirms the trigger is universal: send_status enum = queued/processing/sent/delivered/failed/expired/cancelled/rejected/dead — no 'pending' — so sendReply's INSERT (process-turn-db.ts:253) throws on every assisted/full turn, making every such turn a poison row exactly as claimed.
confirmed.corrected_fix: In the drainAmandaInbound catch, flip the row out of 'processing' the same way the retry branch does, inside its own guarded write so a DB-down error cannot kill the drain: await withAgency(row.agency_id, tx => tx.execute(sql`UPDATE public.amanda_inbound_queue SET status = ${row.attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS ? 'failed' : 'pending'}, next_attempt_at = now() + make_interval(secs => ${backoffSeconds(row.attempts)}), lease_expires_at = NULL, error_message = ${msg.slice(0, 240)} WHERE id = ${row.id}::uuid`)).catch(logOnly) — attempts is already the post-claim count (the RPC increments it at claim), and next_attempt_at is only honored for status='pending', which is why the row must leave 'processing' on error. Defense in depth: make the RPC's stale-lease branch mark rows with attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS as 'failed' instead of re-claiming them, so a worker that dies before its catch runs cannot loop forever either. Separately fix the trigger: sendReply must insert status='queued' (send_status has no 'pending' label) — but the catch-path fix is required regardless, since any persistent model/API/DB error reproduces the poison-row loop.

confirmed.summary: The one-tap/queued booking path has no executor in the live system: in assisted mode a confirmed pending action routes to queueDraft('[confirm booking <echo>]', 'one_tap') (turn.ts:97-99 + modes.ts:58 queue_one_tap), which lands as an ordinary task_type='suggested_reply' dashboard task — and the only live action on that task is approve_dashboard_task, which exclusively SENDS TEXT (verified RPC definition: inserts into send_queue + conversation_messages; it knows nothing about amanda_pending_actions). Nothing ever executes the booking; the pending action expires after 24h. Meanwhile the model is told '(awaiting final one-tap approval by the office — tell them it is being locked in)' (turn.ts:135) and that reply DOES send for real in assisted mode.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Assisted mode: buyer confirms Friday 17:00 → buyer is told 'we're locking it in' → agent approves the queued task → the buyer receives the literal placeholder text '[confirm booking Friday 28 August, 17:00 …]' (or, with the message_body bug, their own 'yes' echoed back) → no booking row is ever created, hold expires, viewing silently never happens. Approval mode has the same dead end for its queued commitment drafts.
confirmed.suggested_fix: P0 scope decision needed: either dial assisted's commitment class down to a human_review_needed task with an explicit 'book it' action wired to executeBooking (new endpoint/RPC), or block assisted mode until the one-tap surface exists; at minimum the drafted text must be a real human-readable message and never a bracket placeholder.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced end-to-end in code: assisted+commitment yields queue_one_tap (modes.ts:58), turn.ts:97-100 queues '[confirm booking <echo>]' via queueDraft, which process-turn-db.ts:261-283 stores as an ordinary task_type='suggested_reply' dashboard task (placeholder in raw_payload.suggested_reply, inbound text in message_body). Grep proves nothing outside amanda-engine/ consumes draft_kind or one_tap; approve_dashboard_task (migration 20260703110345, untouched by the new migration) only COALESCEs edited body/message_body into send_queue+conversation_messages and never references amanda_pending_actions — so approving the task sends the literal bracket placeholder (dashboard pre-fills the draft as the send text) or echoes the buyer's inbound, and no code path ever calls executeBooking in assisted mode; the pending action expires after 24h with no aging→handoff conversion despite design §'ASSISTED pending loop' requiring it. Golden test S8 pins the failure verbatim: reply 'I am locking that in with the office right now' auto-sends (outcome 'sent'), bookings empty, one_tap draft queued with no consumer. One mechanism detail in the finding is wrong but non-refuting: turn.ts:135's '(awaiting final one-tap approval…)' string is unreachable in the queued path (bookingEcho stays null since turn.ts:101 excludes queued results); the model instead sees the unchanged pending_viewing_proposal echo and produces the same false 'locking it in' send. Severity 'important' is fair: engine is env-gated off, migration unapplied, and assisted is a P2 phase — but the P0.5 demo track explicitly allows test agencies to run any mode, making the dead end reachable at ship time. Approval mode shares the no-executor gap for its commitment drafts, though there the conversational reply is also only drafted.
confirmed.corrected_fix: P0 scope decision needed, with one correction to the finding's mechanism: the fix must also account for turn.ts:135's 'awaiting one-tap approval' branch being dead code in the queued path (bookingEcho is never set when result.queued is truthy), so today the model silently invents its own 'locking it in' phrasing. Options: (a) wire a real executor — a dedicated task action (e.g. POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/execute-booking or an approve_dashboard_task branch keyed on raw_payload.draft_kind='one_tap' + pending_action_id stored in raw_payload) that calls the executeBooking path (create_manual_viewing + pending-action resolution) and then sends a human-readable confirmation, plus the design-mandated untapped-after-deadline → handoff conversion; or (b) until that surface exists, have assisted's commitment class route to escalateToHuman/human_review_needed (never a suggested_reply the dashboard will happily send) and give the model an explicit context note that the booking is NOT yet made (populate the queued branch's pendingActionEcho, e.g. 'the office must still confirm — say you are checking with the office, do NOT say it is booked'); at absolute minimum, stop storing a bracket placeholder as raw_payload.suggested_reply on a task whose approve path sends that text verbatim to the buyer.

confirmed.summary: Enable-condition split between EF and worker creates a silent zero-draft state, and the queue has no message-age/mode-at-arrival guard: the EF suppresses W4C whenever amanda_mode is approval/assisted/full (line 279-280) regardless of whether the API worker is actually running — but the worker only exists if AMANDA_ENGINE_ENABLED==='true' at module load (apps/api/src/index.ts:221, evaluated once at boot; env is unset in prod per the rollout plan). Also the EF enqueues EVERY inbound for EVERY agency including mode 'off' (lines 252-269), the drain claims oldest-first (migration line 275, ORDER BY created_at ASC), and processTurnDb reads amanda_mode at PROCESSING time (process-turn-db.ts:48-49) with no check of the row's age.
confirmed.failure_scenario: (a) Christian dials an agency to 'approval' before the Railway env flag is set (or after a deploy where it was dropped): W4C stops drafting, engine never drains → inbound messages get NO draft at all, silently, with rows piling up 'pending'. (b) The EF+migration are deployed with the engine env off for weeks (the documented sequencing): every agency's inbound accumulates in amanda_inbound_queue; when the engine is later enabled and an agency dialed up, weeks-old messages are processed under the CURRENT mode oldest-first — the engine drafts/sends replies to stale conversations as if they just arrived (the 30-min send_queue expiry only guards after the reply is composed).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Gate the EF's W4C suppression on an explicit engine-live signal (or accept double-draft during cutover), and make processTurnDb skip kind message/media rows older than a threshold (e.g. created_at < now()-1h → skip 'stale_inbound') and/or only enqueue when amanda_mode != 'off'.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Every cited mechanic reproduces in the code: EF v3 lines 279-280 suppress W4C on amanda_mode alone with no engine-liveness signal; index.ts:220 creates the drain interval only when AMANDA_ENGINE_ENABLED==='true' at boot (documented as unset in prod); EF lines 252-269 enqueue every inbound for every agency including mode 'off'; the claim RPC (migration line 275) is ORDER BY created_at ASC with no age cutoff and the migration has no queue TTL/prune; process-turn-db.ts:48-49 reads mode at processing time and runTurn gets atMs=Date.now() with no row-age check; the design-mandated sweep alert on old unprocessed rows is explicitly deferred to P1, making both failure states silent. Scenario (a) — mode dialed to approval while env unset/dropped → zero drafts, rows pile pending — is fully accurate and only process discipline prevents it. Scenario (b) holds with one refinement the finding missed: processTurnDb skips mode-'off' rows, so a backlog accumulated while ALL agencies were 'off' self-cleans as 'skipped' once draining starts; the stale-processing danger concentrates in (b1) an agency at approval+ during the env-off window, whose whole backlog is then processed as if fresh (stale drafts in approval; actual stale buyer sends in assisted/full since send_queue's 30-min expiry counts from composition), and (b2) dialing up while old pending rows are still mid-drain (20 rows/20s). That is a narrowing of scenario (b)'s broadest reading, not a refutation — the absence of any age guard, mode filter at enqueue, and liveness gate is real.
confirmed.corrected_fix: Three-part fix, all implementable in the reviewed code: (1) Zero-draft guard — gate the EF's W4C suppression on an explicit engine-liveness signal rather than amanda_mode alone (e.g. a heartbeat row the drain worker updates each tick, or an EF-visible AMANDA_ENGINE_LIVE env set in the same change as the Railway flag); until that signal exists, prefer accepting double-drafting during cutover over silent zero-drafting. (2) Stale-row guard — add created_at to the QueueRow interface in outbox-lib.ts (the table has it and pick_and_claim's RETURNING q.* already returns it) and have processTurnDb skip kind message/media rows with created_at older than a threshold (~1h) with reason 'stale_inbound', so backlogs from any env-off or crash window are never conversationally replayed as fresh. (3) Accumulation hygiene — either skip the enqueue when amanda_mode is 'off' (shadow and up still need it; note this forfeits replay/comparison data for off agencies) or keep enqueueing but pull the design §7 sweep alert on pending rows older than X minutes forward from P1 into P0, so the silent-pile-up state is at least visible.

confirmed.verdict_reason: Verified against both repo and live: the sendReply comment (process-turn-db.ts:243-244) claims "opt-out/window law lives THERE," but the executor — repo v6.7 AND the live deployed version (platform v20, fetched read-only, source v6.6) — enforces only sendBlockedByOptIn (opted_out/blocked, repo lines 227-230); the sole "window" reference is the post-hoc Twilio 63016 failure hint (lines 418-421), i.e. the window is discovered by Twilio rejecting the send, never pre-checked. DESIGN_v1.2 line 67 verbatim requires whatsapp-send-execute to re-check 24h window (60-120s margin), opt-out, kill switch, ai-muted/human-claimed, and ai_disclosure_sent_at at the moment of send, and line 74 requires refusing AI-auto freeform where disclosure is NULL — only the opt-out item is implemented. Before assisted/full runs beyond the is_test demo, implement the design §4 send gate IN whatsapp-send-execute itself — a pre-insert withAgency check narrows but cannot close the race (the insert→drain gap, bounded by the 30-min expiry_at, remains), and the design names the executor as the atomic point. The executor re-checks: (a) 24h window vs last inbound with 60-120s margin, (b) conversations.ai_muted_at/human_claimed_at, (c) ai_disclosure_sent_at NULL-refusal — with (b) and (c) keyed to AI-auto sends only (requested_by='amanda_engine' passed through the send_queue row / EF payload) so human-approved and template sends are unaffected. confirmed.summary: The validator is called with allowLongForm: false unconditionally (turn.ts:155, 35-word/3-sentence cap), while the system prompt explicitly invites longer replies ('Longer only when they asked a broad question or you're summarizing a property they requested', prompt.ts:40) and the design §10 length law grants ≤120 words for exactly those cases — the engine has no classifier wiring the long-form exception.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Buyer asks 'tell me about this villa' → the model produces the invited ~60-word summary → lint fails too_long → one constrained retry ('Keep it short') → if still >35 words the turn escalates to the human queue; broad questions systematically degrade to clipped answers or needless escalations.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wire a deterministic long-form trigger (e.g. inbound interrogative + length, or a get_property_details tool call this turn) into the allowLongForm flag.
confirmed.verdict_reason: All claims verified against the code: turn.ts:155 is the sole production caller of validateDraft and hardcodes allowLongForm: false; validators.ts builds the full long-form mechanism (LONG_MAX_WORDS=120, LintOptions comment naming the exact §10 exception cases, unit tests for allowLongForm:true) but nothing ever passes true; prompt.ts:40 actively invites longer replies for broad questions/property summaries; design §10 (doc line 119) grants ≤120 words for those cases. The gates.ts classifier is social/fact_bearing only — no long-form trigger exists, and no comment marks this as deferred. Failure logic reproduces: an invited ~60-word summary trips too_long/too_many_sentences, burns the single constrained retry to clip it, and escalates if the retry stays long — systematic degradation of exactly the turns the prompt and design promise long-form for. Severity minor is correct: fail direction is safe (over-strict, never over-loose).
confirmed.corrected_fix: Wire a deterministic long-form eligibility check into turn.ts's judge closure instead of the hardcoded false, using signals already available at that point: (a) loop.toolEvents contains a successful get_property_details call this turn (the "requested property summary" case), or (b) the inbound is a broad question — interrogative inbound.text over a small word threshold with no pending confirmation in play, or (c) the turn is the re-engagement nudge / an office-answer relay (both already deterministically known to the orchestrator via lead-state/ticket context). Per design §10 also gate on "never two long messages in a row" — require the previous Amanda outbound (available in ctx.recentTurns) to be under the short cap before granting allowLongForm. Add a golden scenario where a broad property question yields a ~60-word grounded summary that passes the law, so the seam stays wired.

confirmed.summary: Context assembly duplicates and mislabels turns: the EF inserts the inbound into conversation_messages BEFORE enqueueing, so loadWorld's last-20 query (lines 63-68) includes the new message in recentTurns AND buildUserContext repeats it in <new_buyer_message>; and all non-inbound rows map to role 'amanda' (lines 112-115) even though live outbound rows are frequently human-sent (sent_by='agent', src operator_approved — verified live: 12 of 14 outbound rows) and TurnContext already supports role 'agent'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Every turn the model sees the buyer's newest message twice (mild quality/token cost); after an agent manually approves edited replies, the engine attributes those human words to itself — e.g. it will 'remember' having made a promise the human agent made and phrase continuity around it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Exclude provider_message_id = row.provider_message_id from recentTurns; map sent_by IN ('agent','aivena-operator', …) → role 'agent'.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Both mechanisms reproduce logically and against live data. (1) Duplication: the proposed EF inserts the inbound into conversation_messages (index.v3-proposed.ts ~line 218) and enqueues amanda_inbound_queue only after that insert succeeds (line 252), so loadWorld's last-20 query (process-turn-db.ts:63-68) always includes the new message; recentTurns flows untouched through turn.ts:132-139 into buildUserContext, which renders it in <recent_messages> and repeats the same text in <new_buyer_message> (prompt.ts:107-113). No dedup exists anywhere, and the query doesn't even SELECT provider_message_id so nothing downstream could filter. golden/harness.ts:114 (recentTurns: [] with inbound passed separately) proves the intended contract is history-excludes-fresh-inbound. (2) Role mislabel: process-turn-db.ts:112-115 maps all non-inbound rows to 'amanda'; TurnContext (prompt.ts:17) declares 'agent' but nothing produces it. Live DB verified read-only: 14 outbound rows, 12 with sent_by='agent' whose raw_payload.source is operator_approved/operator_reengage with operator_email — human-mediated sends, exactly the finding's 12-of-14. It is actually worse than stated: in the engine's own 'approval' launch mode every reply is operator-approved (sent_by='agent'), so all engine-era outbound — including operator-EDITED text — would be attributed to Amanda, conflicting with design doc line 87 ("human turns ingested as ground truth overriding Amanda's priors"). Severity 'minor' is fair: prompt-quality/attribution issue, not a safety breach (validators and the send gate still govern output).
confirmed.corrected_fix: In loadWorld (process-turn-db.ts:63-68), add sent_by and provider_message_id to the SELECT and exclude the row being processed in SQL: SELECT direction, content, sent_at, sent_by FROM conversation_messages WHERE conversation_id = ${row.conversation_id}::uuid AND provider_message_id IS DISTINCT FROM ${row.provider_message_id} ORDER BY sent_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20. Then map roles at lines 112-115: direction === 'inbound' → 'buyer'; sent_by === 'agent' → 'agent' (the only human marker observed live — 'aivena-operator' from the original suggestion does not exist; engine/system sends carry 'send-pusher'/'system'/etc.); everything else → 'amanda'. Optionally prefix [agent] turns in prompt.ts as a teammate's words so the model treats them as ground truth per design §hand-back, but the loader change alone fixes both the duplication and the misattribution.

confirmed.summary: The file contains a raw NUL byte (0x00 at offset 601) as the hash delimiter inside the template string (`${conversationId}\x00${providerMessageId}`), which makes git treat the source file as BINARY — `git diff` shows 'Bin 0 -> 687 bytes' for it, so the file is un-reviewable/un-mergeable as text and some toolchains may strip or mangle the byte silently (changing every turn_id).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Any future edit of this file can't be diffed; an editor or formatter that normalizes the NUL would silently change turnId output, breaking idempotency continuity for in-flight rows (send_queue idempotency keys and amanda_turn_usage turn_ids would no longer match prior hashes).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use the escape sequence '�' (or any printable delimiter like '\n') in the source instead of a literal NUL byte; the digest changes either way only if the delimiter byte changes, so fix it before the migration is applied and anything durable references turn ids.
confirmed.verdict_reason: Reproduced every claim byte-for-byte: turn-id.ts is 687 bytes with exactly one raw 0x00 at offset 601, inside the hash template literal `${conversationId}<NUL>${providerMessageId}`; `git diff --stat main...HEAD` shows `Bin 0 -> 687 bytes` and `git diff` shows "Binary files ... differ", so the tracked file is un-diffable/un-mergeable as text. The hazard is real: the Read tool itself renders the NUL invisibly (looks like a space), turn-id.test.ts pins no exact digest (only structural properties), so a formatter/editor normalizing the byte would pass all tests while silently changing every turnId — which feeds the durable outbox idempotency key (`amanda-engine:${turnId(...)}`, process-turn-db.ts:246) and amanda_turn_usage turn_id (line 312). Severity minor is correct since the migration is unapplied and the engine is gated off, so nothing durable references turn ids yet.
confirmed.corrected_fix: In /Users/christianscholte/aivena-p2am/apps/api/src/amanda-engine/turn-id.ts line 13, replace the literal NUL byte with the source escape sequence: .update(`${conversationId}�${providerMessageId}`). The escape produces the identical runtime byte, so every digest is unchanged (no idempotency impact) while the file becomes pure text again — git diffs normally and no editor can silently mangle it. Add one digest-pinning test (e.g. expect(turnId('c1','SM123')).toBe('turn_<current 32-hex prefix>')) so any future delimiter change fails loudly instead of silently re-keying the outbox. Do this before the migration is applied and anything durable references turn ids.

refuted.summary: Dead normalization in the IBAN/payment screen. screenPaymentDetails builds `compact = draft.replace(/[ ]/g, ' ')` (line 87) — the character class is a single ASCII space replaced by an ASCII space, a no-op. The intended unicode/NBSP-space normalization never happens, so the IBAN screen leans entirely on `\s?` in IBAN_RE, which allows at most ONE whitespace char between 4-char groups.
refuted.why: Refuted by hex dump. Line 87's character class is not an ASCII space: bytes are 2f 5b C2 A0 5d 2f, i.e. /[ ]/g — a non-breaking space (U+00A0) replaced with ASCII space. That is real, intentional NBSP normalization that merely renders invisibly as a space; the reviewer was misled by visual rendering. Additionally, JS \s already matches all Unicode whitespace (NBSP, thin space, etc.), so single exotic-space separators between IBAN groups match IBAN_RE even without the replace. The only genuine evasion (dot/double-space separators with no PAYMENT_WORDS token nearby) stems from IBAN_RE permitting at most one \s between groups — a separate, narrower hardening opportunity, not the claimed dead normalization.
